question.problem:
Given the orthogonal basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ and the vector $x$ below, find the value of $6{x}_{1},$ where ${x}_{1}$ is the first component of $[x]_{B}.$

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 12\end{aligned}]\},\,x=[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 8\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${q}_{1},\,{q}_{2}.$ 

Since $B$ is an orthogonal basis, we have that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$, where ${x}_{i}=\frac{x\cdot {q}_{i}}{{q}_{i}\cdot {q}_{i}}.$ Computing ${x}_{1},$ we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{x\cdot {q}_{1}}{{q}_{1}\cdot {q}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{(-9)\cdot 4+8\cdot 2}{{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-36+16}{16+4} \\  & =\frac{-20}{20} \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
6{x}_{1}=6\cdot (-1)=-6.
$$
